external_actions.what_that_means: No case in this phase pushes, opens, merges, deploys, submits or tags anything. Every external effect is declared to script-codex-ship.sh, which records the intent and refuses to act — MSG_CODEX_SHIP_MODE=live is itself a refusal path with its own eval. Ordering is proved from the run's own event journal rather than from a real remote.

bindings.concern: external actions and the one-PR terminal
bindings.what_it_does: Turns every reach outside the repository into a declared intent checked against the calling skill's canonical authority, so the properties that matter are machine-checkable instead of prose. It refuses five shapes: an actor taking an action it does not own (above all pre-merge merging, pushing or deploying — exit 4), a PR on a failing verdict (exit 5), a second PR from one gate run (exit 6), OPEN-PR reaching for `gh pr create` while kermit is available or falling back to it without naming the degradation (exit 7), and any request to perform the effect for real (exit 10).

bindings.concern: sanctioned writes per skill and per mode
bindings.what_it_does: The sanctioned-write list is enforced per mode, not per skill, because collapsing the modes would quietly hand a normal gate run its init authority. A pre-merge gate writes its own artifacts and nothing else; `--init` adds only the config it just got approval for; `--update-criticality` adds only test markers. Merge's staging, production and init lists are separate the same way, and `devkit/PLATFORMS.md` gets its own refusal because it is the one file merge --init explicitly never writes.

bindings.concern: release-gate ordering — lock timing, double confirmation, pinned sign-off, rollback
bindings.what_it_does: Merge's safety lives in the order, and nothing about a Codex run makes an order checkable — so the run's own event journal becomes the evidence. It refuses every ordering that keeps the checks while losing the guarantee: the lock not read before the gates (exit 3), the lock taken before they clear or the merge running unlocked or the lock left held (exits 4 and 8), a missing, out-of-order, collapsed, misowned or ignored-cancel gate and a merge on absent or red CI (exit 5), a sign-off naming anything but the verified commit (exit 6), and a rollback that ran without being offered and approved (exit 7).

bindings.concern: human gates stay mandatory and main-thread owned
bindings.what_it_does: Each pre-merge init approval and each merge gate is exercised through the fail-closed envelope: it holds the run with its exact option set, refuses an answer outside that set, stops on a dismissal with no default, and blocks rather than assuming when no question surface can hold it. Merge's gates are root-owned, so the relay — which exists for leaf-owned eng gates — refuses them outright, and the sequencer rejects any gate a child thread recorded.

The losing text may not win on Codex. A store submission is submitted, never live: a submission terminal claiming liveness is refused, while the canonical compounds that say the opposite (`live-to-users`, the `live_status` seam) are removed before the check rather than caught by it. A green release must also state the outcome it reached — success.

The ruling is that the security protocol and the safety floor win over tooling-detection's `warn`. Both winning texts are mirrored byte-for-byte and asserted verbatim on the Codex side, including the two clauses that carry the ruling: there is no green-gate path without secret-scan coverage, and the blocker is not declinable at gate time.

The canonical fix wired the read into merge before deploy and verify — read-only, warn-and-proceed when absent. The Codex package asserts that wiring is present at all three sites rather than assuming the mirror carried it.

bindings.concern: both init protocols consume the doctor detector
bindings.what_it_does: The helper was previously claimed by its header with no call edge. The canonical fix made both init protocols run it instead of hand-deriving the probes; the Codex evals assert the call edge in both protocols and the byte identity of the helper, so the dead-code reading cannot return through the mirror.

bindings.concern: manifest-driven pipeline and verdict emission parity
bindings.what_it_does: The pipeline plan, the diff surface, test-selection tiering, sign-off coverage, CI grading, release identity and the verdict document are all produced by helpers that exist once and are mirrored byte-for-byte. The differential layer replays the real Claude fixtures against the Codex package and compares exit code, stdout and artifact bytes; the verdict is additionally checked for byte-stability across successive invocations, so a relayed verdict cannot differ from the artifact.

evals.bijection: the 9 pre-merge and 9 merge eval IDs named by the two compatibility maps, one case each, no extras

layers.2: adapter contract, runtime bindings, gates and write boundaries
layers.4: differential artifact parity against the existing Claude fixtures

honesty.why: Layers 0/2/4 prove packaging, the release-gate bindings, the write boundaries and deterministic artifact parity for real and offline. They do not prove that a model driving the adapter reaches these gates in the first place, phrases them canonically, or records the journal faithfully — a run that never calls the sequencer is not caught by the sequencer. Ten of the eighteen new cases carry an explicit `residual:` line naming what is still unproven, and the runner reports runtime proof as not-run until the layer 3 suite has executed.
